_comment: Storage-shaped exemption registry for bin/check_contract_casing.py — Architect Decision 18.
The ratchet counts snake_case occurrences in typespec contracts. Most are drift. Some are
NOT: a field whose wire name is *required* to equal a database column name, because the
database is canonical and the contract is describing the stored shape rather than a
consumer-facing surface. Those are exempt — but ONLY when declared here, with the column
they mirror and the PR that introduced them. An undeclared snake_case field is a violation
whether or not it sits in the CDLC family.
Every entry must name a real `table.column`. That requirement is the point: it forces the
justification to be checkable rather than asserted, and it is what stops this file from
becoming a suppression list. If a field has no underlying column — because it is a derived
aggregate, or mirrors a document key rather than a column — it does not belong here and
must be renamed or argued separately.
Governed by Decision 13 condition 2: cite the PR and the column. No silent growth — adding
an entry lowers the effective floor by one, so growth here is as visible as a floor bump.
`contract` scopes the exemption to one file. Omit it only when a field genuinely appears
storage-shaped in several contracts; scope it wherever you can, because an unscoped entry
would exempt an unrelated same-named field elsewhere.

entries.rationale: DBA ruling dffa404e condition 1: distinct independently-minted identity, and the contract must name the column it mirrors or it misdescribes the stored shape. Column created by DRAFT-068.

DBA ruling dffa404e condition 2: a text REFERENCE, not a parent. The wire name is the column name because the whole point of the ruling is that it is a reference to the existing named-session convention, not a renamed consumer concept. Scoped to this contract: session_id elsewhere is not automatically storage-shaped.
DBA ruling dffa404e and 66289b009: the join key from the Tier-2 marker to the single Tier-3 census report. Non-null exactly when sampled.

Column created by DRAFT-068. Named source_namespace rather than `namespace` because the latter is a reserved TypeSpec keyword, and because it is the existing house convention in the doctrine transition records.
Column created by DRAFT-068; carries the Conduit ticket an execution ran against.
Column created by DRAFT-068; the generic work-item identity where no ticket applies.

B1/B3 provenance: the content-addressed doctrine snapshot in force. Column created by DRAFT-068. Scoped to this contract — this name also appears in the pre-existing keychain contracts, which this entry does not excuse.
Column created by DRAFT-068. The seven census categories are all relative to the card set in force, so a finding cannot be re-evaluated without it.

_deliberately_not_registered.why: No underlying column. These are DERIVED values computed by buildCensusReportIndex at read time — the A2b read model is not a projection of a table, it is a computation over canonical rows. There is no `table.column` to cite, so the registry's own entry schema refuses them, and they stay counted as violations. Renaming them is a wire-shape decision (the endpoint serialises the index object directly, so the contract and the response must agree) and is NOT taken unilaterally here. Raised to the Architect as a category the ruling did not anticipate.

No PG column. Mirrors keychain InstanceManifest.asset_id, which is a MongoDB document field, not a column in the nexus database. Decision 18's registry is scoped to `table.column` storage shape; a Mongo document key is a different justification and should be ruled on rather than assumed.
Names a TABLE (nebula.schema_version), not a column. The census envelope's schema_version is a document-format marker with no stored counterpart. Not registered.
